title: English Wikipedia article: Affine connection
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":607690,"ns":0,"title":"Affine connection","extract":"In differential geometry, an affine connection is a geometric object on a smooth manifold which connects nearby tangent spaces, so it permits tangent vector fields to be differentiated as if they were functions on the manifold with values in a fixed vector space. title: English Wikipedia article: Carlyle circle
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":39453637,"ns":0,"title":"Carlyle circle","extract":"In mathematics, a Carlyle circle is a certain circle in a coordinate plane associated with a quadratic equation; it is named after Thomas Carlyle. title: English Wikipedia article: Carré du champ operator
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":74738076,"ns":0,"title":"Carré du champ operator","extract":"The carré du champ operator (French for square of a field operator) is a bilinear, symmetric operator from analysis and probability theory. title: English Wikipedia article: Accessible quasi-category
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":79967502,"ns":0,"title":"Accessible quasi-category","extract":"In mathematics, especially category theory, an accessible quasi-category is a quasi-category in which each object is an ind-object on some small quasi-category. English Wikipedia article: Dominance order
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":14834796,"ns":0,"title":"Dominance order","extract":"In discrete mathematics, dominance order (synonyms: dominance ordering, majorization order, natural ordering) is a partial order on the set of partitions of a positive integer n that plays an important role in algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, especially in the context of symmetric functions and representation theory of the symmetric group.","description":"Discrete math concept","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Derivative of the exponential map
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":44135401,"ns":0,"title":"Derivative of the exponential map","extract":"In the theory of Lie groups, the exponential map is a map from the Lie algebra g of a Lie group G into G. title: English Wikipedia article: Arithmetico-geometric sequence
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":37668047,"ns":0,"title":"Arithmetico-geometric sequence","extract":"In mathematics, an arithmetico-geometric sequence is the result of element-by-element multiplication of the elements of a geometric progression with the corresponding elements of an arithmetic progression. title: English Wikipedia article: Hilbert–Burch theorem
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":33800100,"ns":0,"title":"Hilbert–Burch theorem","extract":"In mathematics, the Hilbert–Burch theorem describes the structure of some free resolutions of a quotient of a local or graded ring in the case that the quotient has projective dimension 2. title: English Wikipedia article: Cyclic surgery theorem
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":29580519,"ns":0,"title":"Cyclic surgery theorem","extract":"In three-dimensional topology, a branch of mathematics, the cyclic surgery theorem states that, for a compact, connected, orientable, irreducible three-manifold M whose boundary is a torus T, if M is not a Seifert-fibered space and r,s are slopes on T such that their Dehn fillings have cyclic fundamental group, then the distance between r and s (the minimal number of times that two simple closed curves in T representing r and s must intersect) is at most 1. Consequently, there are at most three Dehn fillings of M with cyclic fundamental group.","description":"Limitation on the Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with cyclic fundamental groups","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Furstenberg boundary
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":45320987,"ns":0,"title":"Furstenberg boundary","extract":"In mathematics, specifically harmonic analysis and probability theory, the Furstenberg boundary is a notion of boundary associated with a group. title: English Wikipedia article: Chain complex
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":138404,"ns":0,"title":"Chain complex","extract":"In mathematics, a chain complex is an algebraic structure that consists of a sequence of abelian groups (or modules) and a sequence of homomorphisms between consecutive groups such that the image of each homomorphism is contained in the kernel of the next. title: English Wikipedia article: Convex polygon
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":660019,"ns":0,"title":"Convex polygon","extract":"In geometry, a convex polygon is a polygon that is the boundary of a convex set. title: English Wikipedia article: Alexander duality
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":3108888,"ns":0,"title":"Alexander duality","extract":"In mathematics, Alexander duality refers to a duality theory initiated by a result of J. title: English Wikipedia article: Amicable triple
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":59747263,"ns":0,"title":"Amicable triple","extract":"In mathematics, an amicable triple is a set of three different numbers so related that the restricted sum of the divisors of each is equal to the sum of the other two numbers.\nIn another equivalent characterization, an amicable triple is a set of three different numbers so related that the sum of the divisors of each is equal to the sum of the three numbers.","description":"Mathematics","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Associative property
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1335,"ns":0,"title":"Associative property","extract":"In mathematics, the associative property is a property of some binary operations that rearranging the parentheses in an expression will not change the result. title: English Wikipedia article: Cantor function
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":320819,"ns":0,"title":"Cantor function","extract":"In mathematics, the Cantor function is an example of a  function that is continuous, but not absolutely continuous. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":14599476,"ns":0,"title":"Casey's theorem","extract":"In mathematics, Casey's theorem, also known as the generalized Ptolemy's theorem, is a theorem in Euclidean geometry named after the Irish mathematician John Casey. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1460717,"ns":0,"title":"Betweenness problem","extract":"Betweenness is an algorithmic problem in order theory about ordering a collection of items subject to constraints that some items must be placed between others. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":677191,"ns":0,"title":"Differential (mathematics)","extract":"In mathematics, differential refers to several related notions derived from the early days of calculus, put on a rigorous footing, such as infinitesimal differences and the derivatives of functions.\nThe term is used in various branches of mathematics such as calculus, differential geometry, algebraic geometry and algebraic topology.","description":"Mathematical notion of infinitesimal difference","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Elementary class
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1284226,"ns":0,"title":"Elementary class","extract":"In model theory, a branch of mathematical logic, an elementary class (or axiomatizable class) is a class consisting of all structures satisfying a fixed first-order theory.","description":"Class in model theory","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Chirp Z-transform
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":241431,"ns":0,"title":"Chirp Z-transform","extract":"The chirp Z-transform (CZT) is a generalization of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). title: English Wikipedia article: Gelfand pair
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":3018619,"ns":0,"title":"Gelfand pair","extract":"In mathematics, a Gelfand pair is a pair (G, K ) consisting of a group G and a subgroup K (called an Euler subgroup of G) that satisfies a certain property on restricted representations. title: English Wikipedia article: Vietoris–Rips filtration
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":73475847,"ns":0,"title":"Vietoris–Rips filtration","extract":"In topological data analysis, the Vietoris–Rips filtration (sometimes shortened to \"Rips filtration\") is the collection of nested Vietoris–Rips complexes on a metric space created by taking the sequence of Vietoris–Rips complexes over an increasing scale parameter. title: English Wikipedia article: Arithmetic derivative
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":16838651,"ns":0,"title":"Arithmetic derivative","extract":"In number theory, the Lagarias arithmetic derivative or number derivative is a function defined for integers, based on prime factorization, by analogy with the product rule for the derivative of a function that is used in mathematical analysis.\nThere are many versions of \"arithmetic derivatives\", including the one discussed in this article (the Lagarias arithmetic derivative), such as Ihara's arithmetic derivative and Buium's arithmetic derivatives.","description":"Function defined on integers in number theory","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Bounded variation
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":330673,"ns":0,"title":"Bounded variation","extract":"In mathematical analysis, a function of bounded variation, also known as BV function, is a real-valued function whose total variation is bounded (finite): the graph of a function having this property is well behaved in a precise sense. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":80072866,"ns":0,"title":"Asymptotic geometry","extract":"Asymptotic geometry, also known as asymptotic geometric analysis or high-dimensional geometry, is a field of mathematics that investigates the geometric properties of finite-dimensional objects, such as convex bodies and normed spaces, as the dimension tends to infinity. title: English Wikipedia article: Monotone convergence theorem
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":146263,"ns":0,"title":"Monotone convergence theorem","extract":"In real analysis, the monotone convergence theorem is any of a number of related theorems proving, under certain conditions, the convergence of monotonic sequences, i.e. sequences that are non-increasing, or non-decreasing.","description":"Theorems on the convergence of bounded monotonic sequences","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Church–Turing thesis
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":6854,"ns":0,"title":"Church–Turing thesis","extract":"In computability theory, the Church–Turing thesis is a thesis about the nature of computable functions. title: English Wikipedia article: Auslander–Buchsbaum theorem
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":30774055,"ns":0,"title":"Auslander–Buchsbaum theorem","extract":"In commutative algebra, the Auslander–Buchsbaum theorem states that regular local rings are unique factorization domains.\nThe theorem was first proved by Maurice Auslander and David Buchsbaum (1959).","description":"Algebraic theorem","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":33677222,"ns":0,"title":"Convex space","extract":"In mathematics, a convex space (or barycentric algebra) is a space in which it is possible to take convex combinations of any finite set of points.","description":"Type of mathematical space","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: (B, N) pair
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1772133,"ns":0,"title":"(B, N) pair","extract":"In mathematics, a (B, N) pair is a structure on groups of Lie type that allows one to give uniform proofs of many results, instead of giving a large number of case-by-case proofs. title: English Wikipedia article: Basis (linear algebra)
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":18420,"ns":0,"title":"Basis (linear algebra)","extract":"In mathematics, a set B of elements of  a vector space V is called a basis (pl.: bases) if every element of V can be written in a unique way as a finite linear combination of elements of B. The coefficients of this linear combination are referred to as components or coordinates of the vector with respect to B. The elements of a basis are called basis vectors.\nEquivalently, a set B is a basis if its elements are linearly independent and every element of V is a linear combination of elements of B. In other words, a basis is a linearly independent spanning set.","description":"Set of vectors used to define coordinates","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":71514588,"ns":0,"title":"Approximate fibration","extract":"In algebraic topology, a branch of mathematics, an approximate fibration is a sort of fibration such that the homotopy lifting property holds only approximately. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":289860,"ns":0,"title":"Alignments of random points","extract":"The study of alignments of random points in a plane seeks to discover subsets of points that occupy an approximately straight line within a larger set of points that are randomly placed in a planar region.\nStudies have shown that such near-alignments occur by chance with greater frequency than one might intuitively expect.","description":"Phenomenon in statistics","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Bernstein polynomial
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":340136,"ns":0,"title":"Bernstein polynomial","extract":"In the mathematical field of numerical analysis, a Bernstein polynomial is a polynomial expressed as a linear combination of Bernstein basis polynomials. title: English Wikipedia article: Decomposition of a module
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":61406091,"ns":0,"title":"Decomposition of a module","extract":"In abstract algebra, a decomposition of a module is a way to write a module as a direct sum of modules. title: English Wikipedia article: Behrend sequence
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":59915725,"ns":0,"title":"Behrend sequence","extract":"In number theory, a Behrend sequence is an integer sequence whose multiples include almost all integers. title: English Wikipedia article: Global analysis
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":42027498,"ns":0,"title":"Global analysis","extract":"In mathematics, global analysis, also called analysis on manifolds, is the study of the global and topological properties of differential equations on manifolds and vector bundles. title: English Wikipedia article: Koecher–Vinberg theorem
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":37016909,"ns":0,"title":"Koecher–Vinberg theorem","extract":"In operator algebra, the Koecher–Vinberg theorem is a reconstruction theorem for real Jordan algebras. title: English Wikipedia article: Euler spiral
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":19107713,"ns":0,"title":"Euler spiral","extract":"An Euler spiral is a curve whose curvature changes linearly with its curve length (the curvature of a circular curve is equal to the reciprocal of the radius). title: English Wikipedia article: Exponential field
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":21313650,"ns":0,"title":"Exponential field","extract":"In mathematics, an exponential field is a field with a further unary operation that is a homomorphism from the field's additive group to its multiplicative group. title: English Wikipedia article: Epsilon calculus
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":11027904,"ns":0,"title":"Epsilon calculus","extract":"In logic, Hilbert's epsilon calculus is an extension of a formal language by the epsilon operator, where the epsilon operator substitutes for quantifiers in that language as a method leading to a proof of consistency for the extended formal language. title: English Wikipedia article: Harmonic tensors
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":72320451,"ns":0,"title":"Harmonic tensors","extract":"In this article spherical functions are replaced by polynomials that have been well known in electrostatics since the time of Maxwell and associated with multipole moments. In physics, dipole and quadrupole moments typically appear because fundamental concepts of physics are associated precisely with them.","description":"Mathematical objects more general than vectors","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Baer norm
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":4967197,"ns":0,"title":"Baer norm","extract":"In mathematics, in the field of group theory, the norm of a group is the intersection of the normalizers of all its subgroups. title: English Wikipedia article: Category of measurable spaces
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":75966255,"ns":0,"title":"Category of measurable spaces","extract":"In mathematics, the category of measurable spaces, often denoted Meas, is the category whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are measurable maps.\nThis is a category because the composition of two measurable maps is again measurable, and the identity function is measurable.","description":"Category whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are measurable maps","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Cubicity
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":73506350,"ns":0,"title":"Cubicity","extract":"In the mathematical field of graph theory, cubicity is a graph invariant defined to be the smallest dimension such that a graph can be realized as the intersection graph of axis-parallel unit cubes in Euclidean space. Cubicity was introduced by Fred S. Roberts in 1969, along with a related invariant called boxicity that considers the smallest dimension needed to represent a graph as the intersection graph of axis-parallel rectangles in Euclidean space.","description":"Graph invariant defined from axis-parallel unit cubes","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Affine sphere
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":31202259,"ns":0,"title":"Affine sphere","extract":"In affine differential geometry, an affine sphere is a hypersurface for which the affine normals all intersect in a single point The term affine sphere is used because they play an analogous role in affine differential geometry to that of ordinary spheres in Euclidean differential geometry.\nAn affine sphere is called improper or parabolic if all of the affine normals are constant.","description":"Mathematical concept","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Bruhat order
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":10163003,"ns":0,"title":"Bruhat order","extract":"In mathematics, the Bruhat order (also called the strong order, strong Bruhat order, Chevalley order, Bruhat–Chevalley order, or Chevalley–Bruhat order) is a partial order on the elements of a Coxeter group, that corresponds to the inclusion order on Schubert varieties.","description":"Partial order on a Coxeter group","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1925846,"ns":0,"title":"Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation","extract":"In mathematical logic, the Brouwer–Heyting–Kolmogorov interpretation, or BHK interpretation, is an explanation of the meaning of proof in intuitionistic logic, proposed by L. E. J. Brouwer and Arend Heyting, and independently by Andrey Kolmogorov. It is also sometimes called the realizability interpretation, because of the connection with the realizability theory of Stephen Kleene.","description":"Interpretation of intuitionistic logic","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Free lattice
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":10361669,"ns":0,"title":"Free lattice","extract":"In mathematics, in the area of order theory, a free lattice is the free object corresponding to a lattice. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":34260496,"ns":0,"title":"Hadamard product (matrices)","extract":"In mathematics, the Hadamard product (also known as the element-wise product, entrywise product or Schur product) is a binary operation that takes in two matrices of the same dimensions and returns a matrix of the multiplied corresponding elements. title: English Wikipedia article: Bernstein–Sato polynomial
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1636721,"ns":0,"title":"Bernstein–Sato polynomial","extract":"In mathematics, the Bernstein–Sato polynomial is a polynomial related to differential operators, introduced independently by Joseph Bernstein (1971) and Mikio Sato and Takuro Shintani (1972, 1974), Sato (1990). title: English Wikipedia article: Fast-growing hierarchy
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":24947285,"ns":0,"title":"Fast-growing hierarchy","extract":"In computability theory, computational complexity theory and proof theory, a fast-growing hierarchy (also called an extended Grzegorczyk hierarchy, or a Schwichtenberg–Wainer hierarchy) is an ordinal-indexed family of rapidly increasing functions fα: N → N (where N is the set of natural numbers {0, 1, ...}, and α ranges up to some large countable ordinal). A primary example is the Wainer hierarchy, or Löb–Wainer hierarchy, which is an extension to all α < ε0.","description":"Ordinal-indexed family of rapidly increasing functions","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Delta-functor
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":20850491,"ns":0,"title":"Delta-functor","extract":"In homological algebra, a δ-functor between two abelian categories A and B is a collection of functors from A to B together with a collection of morphisms that satisfy properties generalising those of derived functors. A universal δ-functor is a δ-functor satisfying a specific universal property related to extending morphisms beyond \"degree 0\".","description":"Functor between abelian categories","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Classical group
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":10172878,"ns":0,"title":"Classical group","extract":"In mathematics, the classical groups are the matrix groups arising from finite-dimensional vector spaces and from nondegenerate bilinear, sesquilinear, quadratic, and Hermitian forms. In the traditional setting of Lie groups, this includes the real, complex, and quaternionic general linear, special linear, orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic groups, together with their indefinite analogues.","description":"Type of group in mathematics","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Dual cone and polar cone
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":10063937,"ns":0,"title":"Dual cone and polar cone","extract":"Dual cone and polar cone are closely related concepts in convex analysis, a branch of mathematics.","description":"Concepts in convex analysis","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Closure (mathematics)
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":293802,"ns":0,"title":"Closure (mathematics)","extract":"In mathematics, a subset of a larger set is closed under a given operation on the larger set if performing that operation on members of the subset always produces a member of that subset. For example, the natural numbers are closed under addition, but not under subtraction: 1 − 2 is not a natural number, although both 1 and 2 are.","description":"Operation on the subsets of a set","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Big M method
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":27701374,"ns":0,"title":"Big M method","extract":"In operations research, the Big M method is a method of solving linear programming problems using the simplex algorithm.  The Big M method extends the simplex algorithm to problems that contain \"greater-than\" constraints.","description":"Method of solving linear programming problems","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}

title: English Wikipedia article: Barycentric subdivision
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":583651,"ns":0,"title":"Barycentric subdivision","extract":"In mathematics, the barycentric subdivision is a standard way to subdivide a given simplex into smaller ones. title: English Wikipedia article: Cauchy product
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":863791,"ns":0,"title":"Cauchy product","extract":"In mathematics, more specifically in mathematical analysis, the Cauchy product is the discrete convolution of two infinite series. title: English Wikipedia article: Alexandrov space
text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":14609741,"ns":0,"title":"Alexandrov space","extract":"In differential geometry, Alexandrov spaces with curvature ≥ k form a generalization of Riemannian manifolds with sectional curvature ≥ k, where k is some real number. text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":1519880,"ns":0,"title":"Collectively exhaustive events","extract":"In probability theory and logic, a set of events is jointly or collectively exhaustive if at least one of the events must occur.
